clue.text: Drink one for the road

definitions.meaning: a cocktail of brandy, orange liqueur and lemon juice
a one-wheeled passenger car bolted to a motorbike travels the road

explanation.definitionFit: It is both a classic brandy cocktail and the passenger pod attached to a motorcycle.

clue.text: Hat, the sort we use in a storm

indicators.note: a storm tosses things about, so these letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A waterproof hat of the kind worn in foul weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a storm' rearranges SORT WE USE.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou'wester is a waterproof hat with a broad brim at the back.

clue.text: Refuse to quote cases

definitions.meaning: in grammar, to recite a noun's forms in each case

explanation.definitionFit: To decline is to turn down, and in grammar it is to list a noun's case forms.

clue.text: It's a mercy this science has developed

indicators.note: developed means changed form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Thank goodness this branch of science has progressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemistry is the science of substances and their reactions.

clue.text: Oil-producer in old part of Sussex

definitions.meaning: a yellow-flowered crop pressed for oil
Sussex, an English county, was historically divided into six districts with this name

explanation.definitionFit: It is the oilseed crop and also one of the historic districts into which the English county of Sussex was divided.

clue.text: As one in the crowd, Edward is uplifted

indicators.note: the letter for one is placed within the word for the crowd

parts.note: a host is a large crowd
I is the Roman numeral one
Ed is short for Edward

explanation.surface: Edward, carried shoulder-high by a crowd, feels elated.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoisting is raising up, so something hoisted has been lifted aloft.

clue.text: Overbearing or surrendering?

definitions.meaning: read literally, with hands held high, as one does in surrender

explanation.definitionFit: High-handed means imperiously bossy, and someone giving up raises their hands high.

clue.text: To sleep in it is not fitting

indicators.note: the sleep word goes inside the word it

parts.note: to nap is to sleep briefly

explanation.surface: Dozing on the job is inappropriate.
explanation.definitionFit: Inapt means unsuitable or inappropriate.

clue.text: Isn't' it common upholding a queen?

annotationWithheld.why: Isn't it common upholding a queen? (7): AIN'T IT holding A, read upwards, gives TITANIA, but the single word 'upholding' is both the container and the reversal indicator, which the check refuses
annotationWithheld.clue: Isn't' it common upholding a queen?

clue.text: The nymph in the temperance poster

parts.note: dry means teetotal, abstaining from drink
an ad is a poster or advertisement

explanation.surface: The nymph pictured in a temperance campaign poster.
explanation.definitionFit: A dryad is a tree nymph of Greek myth.

clue.text: One closely connected with pop

parts.note: pop is slang for pawning, and a pawnbroker has an old nickname that is also the family term for a parent's brother, closely related to Pop

explanation.surface: A close relative of Dad.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: a father's brother is closely connected to 'pop', and in old slang the pawnbroker, with whom one pops (pawns) goods, has the same nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: A parent's brother is a close relative of Dad, and the word is also old slang for a pawnbroker, to whom you 'pop' things.

clue.text: Show room for provisions, about time!

indicators.note: the storeroom word goes around the word for time

parts.note: a pantry is a room where food is stored
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: A display of a larder, at long last!
explanation.definitionFit: Pageantry is splendid public display and spectacle.

clue.text: Anger in retrospect having to swallow number nine, a sovereign remedy

indicators.note: the reversed word for anger takes the numeral inside it
looking back means the word for anger is read from right to left

parts.note: to rile is to anger
IX is nine in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Looking back on one's rage while taking pill number nine, a cure-all.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' in the clue as filed was an OCR slip for 'a'; 'having' is a link word joining the two halves.
explanation.definitionFit: An elixir is a supposed cure-all, and a sovereign remedy is one held to cure everything.

clue.text: Complained about Lawrence initially being cleared of guilt

indicators.note: the word for complained goes around the initials

parts.note: whined means complained
T. E. are the initials of T. E. Lawrence, Lawrence of Arabia

explanation.surface: Someone moaned that Lawrence was being exonerated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' here means Lawrence's initials, T.E., not the first letter L.
explanation.definitionFit: To whitewash or whiten a name is to clear it of blame.

clue.text: Bowmen of Cambridge beheaded

parts.note: bowmen shoot arrows, and Cambridge without its first letter is Ambridge, the village of a long-running BBC radio farming soap

explanation.surface: Archers from Cambridge are executed.
explanation.walkthrough: Ambridge is the fictional village in the BBC radio soap about the farming Archer family; 'beheaded' takes the C off Cambridge.
explanation.definitionFit: Bowmen are archers, and the family of Ambridge are the radio soap's title family.

clue.text: Free food — dug right in

indicators.note: the letter for right goes inside the word for dug

parts.note: a dug is an animal's teat or udder

explanation.surface: Food handed out free while someone dug the garden right in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dug' looks like a verb but is the noun for an udder or teat.
explanation.definitionFit: A treat is something paid for on another's behalf, such as a meal on the house.

clue.text: Passes over fish in greeting

indicators.note: in an across clue the first piece is placed over, that is before, the next

parts.note: hands means passes over, gives
hake is a sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone passes the fish across while saying hello.
explanation.definitionFit: Clasping and shaking another's hand is a customary greeting.

clue.text: American governor

parts.note: read as a man of the States, i.e. someone American, the phrase also suggests a leading political figure who governs

explanation.surface: A US state governor.
explanation.definitionFit: A statesman is a skilled political leader, and split up it reads as a man of the States.

clue.text: Choose to have spoken of voters

parts.note: to elect is to choose by vote
oral means spoken

explanation.surface: Picking a spoken ballot for the voters.
explanation.definitionFit: Electoral describes things relating to an electorate or elections.

clue.text: Not to order like Byron's critics

definitions.meaning: made in advance rather than tailored for a customer
Byron wrote in English Bards and Scotch Reviewers that every trade needs an apprenticeship save censure: critics all are this

explanation.surface: Off-the-peg goods compared with critics a poet mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ready-made goods are bought off the shelf, and Byron jibed that critics need no training, coming fully formed.

clue.text: Pardon my confession of broodiness?

parts.note: as in 'I am', a first-person admission
nesty, keen to build a nest, describes a broody hen

explanation.surface: Forgive my admission that I feel broody.
explanation.walkthrough: 'my confession of broodiness' is read as the speaker saying 'I am nesty', with I understood; nesty is a playful coinage for wanting to nest.
explanation.definitionFit: An amnesty is a general pardon for offenders.

clue.text: One's drink is outside in the passage

indicators.note: the drink word sits around the letters for one's

parts.note: ale is a beer
one's read as 'one is' gives I and S

explanation.surface: Someone's beer is left outdoors in the corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', I + S, which goes inside ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisle is a walkway between rows of seats.

clue.text: Tool with directions put in box

indicators.note: the directions are put inside the boxing word

parts.note: to spar is to box
NNE, north-north-east, is a compass direction

explanation.surface: A tool kit with instructions packed in a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A spanner is a wrench for turning nuts.

clue.text: Catch the last call

definitions.meaning: in bridge the final bid of the auction fixes the agreement the declarer must make

explanation.definitionFit: One contracts a cold by catching it, and in bridge the final bid settles the undertaking to be made.

clue.text: Island resolved to see you are spoken of

indicators.note: resolved means broken up, so these letters are rearranged
said aloud, the words see, you and are sound like the letters C, U and R

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like CUR
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone decided on a Greek island they'd heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoken' turns 'see you are' into C, U, R; 'resolved' rearranges them with OF.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea.

clue.text: Form of football, the French or Australian variety

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: A kind of football, perhaps the French or the Aussie version.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian Rules is a football code, so the bare word stands for the Australian variety.

clue.text: Concerning bygone meal

parts.note: re means concerning, about
past means bygone

explanation.surface: About a dinner from long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: A repast is a formal word for a meal.

clue.text: Check the ancestral line

definitions.meaning: to stop or stanch a flow
the main line of descent of a family

explanation.definitionFit: To stem is to halt a flow, and a family stem is its line of descent.

clue.text: One listener distressed, but readily recovering

indicators.note: distressed means upset, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A single listener is upset, but soon bounces back.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone resilient bounces back quickly from shocks.

clue.text: This key not that of the door

definitions.text: This key not that of the door

parts.words: This key not that of the door
parts.note: the key meant is a musical scale, not the kind used for a lock, and the key of the door was traditionally given at 21, so this also describes someone under age

explanation.surface: Not the house key but another sort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The key of the door' was traditionally given at 21, so the person without it is under age; a sad musical key has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a musical key with a flattened third, and also a person under age who has not yet got the key of the door.

clue.text: The man for Penelope or Joyce

definitions.meaning: Penelope waited faithfully for her husband, the Roman name for Odysseus

explanation.definitionFit: It is the Latin name of Penelope's wandering husband and the title of Joyce's novel.

clue.text: Railmen working for pop, perhaps

indicators.note: working means being worked over, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Railway workers on the job for a fizzy drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Mineral water, a fizzy soft drink, is an example of pop.
